summary: Initial discovery to understand Skyline's networking constraints for a Private VPC deployment. Main concerns: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, cross-account routing, CIDR conflicts, region constraints (us-west-2 preference), SSO/KMS requirements, and latency/cost tradeoffs. Redwood AE+SE explained high-level options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), default network patterns, and next steps to collect CIDR info and run an SE benchmarking session.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-26
Start time: 14:22 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Eli Thompson (Skyline CTO), Rosa Martinez (Lead Infra), Kevin Liu (Security)

Summary: quick discovery focused on private VPC networking, peering options, and compliance needs.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this and i have maya from our SE team, how's it going?
[00:18] Eli: good thanks, we have a packed agenda, want to make sure we cover network constraints and security first.
[00:34] Maya: great, quick agenda — we'll run through the high-level deployment options (hosted, dedicated, private), then dig into VPC peering, private endpoints, region constraints, and any compliance needs, and then next steps.
[01:05] Rosa: to kick off — we're leaning toward private VPC deployment because of PCI and some reseller contracts that require no public egress. pref is us-west-2 but we do have presence in us-east-1 for DR.
[01:27] Kevin: and from security perspective we need SAML SSO, audit logs, and keys in our KMS/HSM. also need to know about data at rest encryption and access patterns.
[01:50] Jordan: totally, that's usual. quick Q — do you have existing Transit Gateway or AWS Direct Connect we should be aware of?
[02:07] Rosa: we have a TGW and DX at our primary colo, yes. network team prefers Transit Gateway peering for scale but we can do peering if necessary.
[02:26] Maya: ok, good. two main network patterns we recommend: 1) VPC peering / cross-account peering to Redwood-managed VPCs 2) PrivateLink / interface endpoints into Redwood's service endpoints. each has pros and cons — peering is simpler for east-west traffic but CIDR clashes are a pain. PrivateLink gives clean private endpoints per-region but needs ENIs and we route via interface endpoints.
[02:58] Eli: can you elaborate on the CIDR issue? 
[03:10] Maya: sure — if both sides use overlapping CIDR ranges, peering won't work without NAT or re-IP. with Transit Gateway you can do route translations but it adds complexity. PrivateLink avoids that because it's an endpoint service; your VPC talks to an ENI in our account so no CIDR overlap problem.
[03:36] Rosa: hmm, we have a lot of overlapping /16s from old projects, that's likely to be a blocker for peering.
[03:47] Jordan: noted. on region — you mentioned us-west-2 primary, we do support deploying Private control plane and inference nodes in us-west-2. the Dedicated pools and private clusters can be pinned to region.
[04:07] Eli: any limitations re. GPU types or model availability in that region? we plan to run Llama variants and some custom fine-tuned models.
[04:24] Maya: GPU availability can vary — we recommend picking instance families we know are supported (A10G / H100 depending on needed perf), and we can provide a compatibility matrix. some open models require more VRAM so quantization options are possible to reduce footprint.
[04:46] Kevin: and what about egress — will our requests ever go over public internet? we need strictly private egress for some tenants.
[05:00] Jordan: by default Private deployment can be configured with no public egress — traffic stays in your VPC and we push images via an internal pipeline or via customer-managed registries. For hosted API there is public, for Dedicated there are options.
[05:17] Rosa: that sounds right — we want no public internet for inference traffic. also need to confirm audit logs go to our S3 bucket.
[05:28] Maya: we can ship audit logs to your S3 or to a SIEM via Kinesis/Firehose; we support S3 + KMS encryption using your customer-managed KMS key.
[05:42] Eli: what about auth — SAML for console vs API keys for service-to-service?
[05:50] Jordan: yes SAML/SSO for human users, and mTLS or API keys (rotatable) for service-to-service. For Private we can integrate with your IdP for SSO and provision roles via SCIM if needed.
[06:08] Kevin: are there SOC2 or pen test artifacts we can review?
[06:15] Jordan: yes, we'll share SOC2 and our security pack — i'll include them in follow up.
[06:22] Rosa: nice.

[06:40] Maya: jumping into networking details — about peering vs PrivateLink: if you have Transit Gateway that accommodates multiple VPCs and routing policies, we can attach Redwood Private VPCs via TGW attachments. otherwise PrivateLink is clean per-AZ and avoids cross-account route propagation headaches.
[07:05] Rosa: our TGW is fairly locked down; adding attachments requires change control and could add weeks of approvals. private endpoints might be faster.
[07:18] Eli: what about latency differences, do we have numbers?
[07:25] Maya: approximate — for same-region PrivateLink you'll see sub-5ms extra overhead compared to internal infra for small token latencies, but depends on model and batching. Peering via TGW is slightly lower overhead but you get complexity tradeoffs. we can run bench to show numbers on your workload.
[07:46] Jordan: also batching and KV cache locality matter a lot — if you can keep the cache local to the inference nodes in your VPC the throughput improves. if you route across a cross-account link you might see added latencies.
[08:05] Rosa: clarify KV cache — you mean the model's kv cache for attention?
[08:11] Maya: yeah, sorry jargon — the token KV cache (we sometimes say k-v cache), it's important for chat/streaming to keep it local to the serving tier.

[08:30] Eli: for our procurement team — what's the typical procurement timeline for Private deploys?
[08:37] Jordan: varies; small pilots can be 2-4 weeks, full private with contracts and compliance can be 6-12 weeks depending on legal and security review.
[08:47] Kevin: any support SLA tiers?
[08:51] Jordan: yes — enterprise support and premium SLA for Dedicated/Private, we can provide 99.9% uptime SLAs on reserved pools.

[09:12] Rosa: about IP addressing — we will send our current CIDR list, but we likely have overlap. if PrivateLink is the preferred path, are there account limits for ENIs? we have pretty large VPCs.
[09:27] Maya: account ENI limits are AWS account limits, we can coordinate on either reducing endpoints or use an NLB pattern; we also support regional endpoints in high scale setups to reduce per-AZ ENI pressure.
[09:46] Eli: for cross-region — if we have DR in us-east-1, how do failovers work? do you recommend active-active or active-passive?
[09:58] Maya: depends on your RTO/RPO. active-active requires replication of model state and KV caches — that's non-trivial. active-passive with warm standby in us-east-1 is simpler; Redwood can route via policy and fallback to a different region but you'll see higher latencies.

[10:28] Jordan: quick note — we also offer Dedicated reserved pools that run in your VPC or connected VPCs; they give predictable throughput and are simpler from an ops perspective but commit pricing. For POC we often start with a small Dedicated pool or Private trial.
[10:46] Rosa: pricing will be key — procurement needs committed numbers.
[10:52] Jordan: we'll share a pricing sheet with examples for bursty vs steady workloads.

[11:10] Kevin: security controls — do you support customer-managed keys for data at rest?
[11:16] Maya: yes, we support CMKs and HSM-backed (bring-your-own) options for Private deployments. logs and model artifacts can be encrypted with your key.
[11:28] Eli: do we need to open inbound ports for the endpoints?
[11:33] Maya: for PrivateLink you'll create interface endpoints in your VPC which creates ENIs — no public open ports are required; peering similarly routes privately. we do need certain egress to Redwood control plane for orchestration but that can be done via private endpoints or via an SSM-like agent minimal egress.

[12:00] Rosa: can we run a benchmark with sample workload and models? we want to measure p99 latencies for chat and throughput for batch embeddings.
[12:10] Maya: absolutely — we'll define a bench plan: sample prompts, concurrency, model versions. maya: i'll run it or our infra bench team will.
[12:22] Jordan: action — send bench runbook and collect your workloads.

[12:40] Eli: about compliance, we may need additional attestations — is Redwood SOC2 Type II available?
[12:47] Jordan: yes, SOC2 is available; we will attach the report.

[13:05] Rosa: curious about network monitoring — will we get per-route telemetry?
[13:11] Maya: yes our console exposes per-route and per-model metrics, but for Private we can also stream VPC flow logs and provide traces to your tracing backend.

[13:30] Kevin: any blockers on our side? 
[13:34] Rosa: main blocker is CIDR overlap and TGW change control. if PrivateLink is feasible, that removes months of approvals.
[13:45] Jordan: understood. we'll prioritize PrivateLink as path-of-least-resistance for the POC.

[14:05] Maya: last bit — for model compatibility and quantization, we'll send a compatibility matrix. sometimes customers choose a quantized variant to reduce GPU needs; that trades off a small quality delta.
[14:24] Eli: that's fine as long as we profile the quality metric.

[14:40] Jordan: ok wrap up — next steps and owners: i'll send SOC2 + architecture diagram, maya will prepare bench plan and recommend instance families, rosa will send CIDR + TGW change window. schedule technical deep dive for next week?
[14:58] Rosa: next week works for an SE deep dive, preferable Wed morning.
[15:06] Jordan: i'll follow up with calendar invite and share artifacts.
[15:12] Kevin: thanks everyone.

End transcript.
notes: Reference docs mentioned: Private deployment diagram (link to be shared), SOC2 bundle, bench runbook. Customer prefers PrivateLink to avoid TGW changes. POC likely next step.
